text: In a feedforward layer a = f(Wa + b), what fraction of the operations are matrix MACs, and why does that matter for photonics?
choices: About 50%, so photonics must also accelerate the activation functions
More than 99% (e.g. 99.83% in an MNIST MLP), so accelerating only the matrix multiply addresses essentially all of the arithmetic
Under 10%; most operations are the nonlinear activations
explanation: The MAC-to-activation ratio is N_{l-1} (hundreds to tens of thousands): an MNIST MLP is 99.83% MACs and a GPT-3-class layer has ~1.8e9 MACs against ~1e5 pointwise ops. So an optical accelerator that speeds only W*a still covers nearly all the arithmetic; activations are cheap and scale only as O(N).
